ucs.title: [LLM] APT32 (OceanLotus) DLL side-loading via abused signed Symantec/McAfee/Avast binaries from user-writable paths
ucs.description: Hunts OceanLotus's signature initial-execution chain: dropping a legitimate signed third-party security/utility binary (rastlsc.exe, McOmonHost.exe, wsc_proxy.exe, SyLog.exe, gup.exe, GoogleUpdate.exe) into %APPDATA%, %TEMP%, %PUBLIC%, %ProgramData% or Downloads alongside a malicious sibling DLL that the signed loader resolves first. APT32 has used this pattern persistently across Denis/KOMPROGO/METALJACK campaigns to evade application-control and signature-based detection.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("rastlsc.exe","mcomonhost.exe","wsc_proxy.exe","sylog.exe","gup.exe","googleupdate.exe","mcoemcpy.exe","mctray.exe","goopdate.exe") AND NOT (Processes.process_path IN ("*\\Program Files\\*","*\\Program Files (x86)\\*","*\\Windows\\System32\\*","*\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*")) AND (Processes.process_path IN ("*\\Users\\*\\AppData\\*","*\\Users\\*\\Downloads\\*","*\\Windows\\Temp\\*","*\\Users\\Public\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*","*\\Temp\\*")) by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | where firstTime != ""
ucs.kql:
// APT32 abused signed binaries — names normalised to lower case
let ApacheList = dynamic(["rastlsc.exe","mcomonhost.exe","wsc_proxy.exe","sylog.exe","gup.exe","googleupdate.exe","mcoemcpy.exe","mctray.exe","goopdate.exe"]);
let SuspectProcs = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ (ApacheList)
    | where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files"
    | where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)"
    | where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32"
    | where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\SysWOW64"
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\", @"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\Public\", @"\ProgramData\")
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessId, ProcessCommandLine,
              ParentFile = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
// Confirm the side-loaded DLL is a sibling in the same writable directory and NOT a Microsoft path
SuspectProcs
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName endswith ".dll"
    | project DllTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId, LoadedDll = FileName,
              LoadedDllPath = FolderPath, LoadedDllSHA256 = SHA256
) on DeviceId, $left.ProcessId == $right.InitiatingProcessId
| where LoadedDllPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\"
| where LoadedDllPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files"
| where tolower(LoadedDllPath) == tolower(FolderPath)        // sibling DLL — classic side-load layout
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentFile, ParentCmd, LoadedDll, LoadedDllPath, LoadedDllSHA256, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
// Sentinel — SecurityEvent 4688 lacks reliable image-load context, so we score on signed-binary launch from writable path + non-system parent
let ApacheList = dynamic(["rastlsc.exe","mcomonhost.exe","wsc_proxy.exe","sylog.exe","gup.exe","googleupdate.exe","mcoemcpy.exe","mctray.exe","goopdate.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ProcLower = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where ProcLower in (ApacheList)
| where NewProcessName !startswith @"C:\Program Files"
| where NewProcessName !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32"
| where NewProcessName !startswith @"C:\Windows\SysWOW64"
| where NewProcessName has_any (@"\AppData\", @"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\Public\", @"\ProgramData\")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentImage = ParentProcessName, LogonId = SubjectLogonId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: APT32 OceanLotus DLL Side-Load Via Signed Vendor Binary From User-Writable Path
id: 9e3e0c12-3a8e-4d6a-bd31-7ab0f6c8e151
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects execution of a small set of legitimate signed third-party binaries
  (Symantec rastlsc.exe, McAfee McOmonHost.exe, Avast wsc_proxy.exe,
  Sygate SyLog.exe, Notepad++ gup.exe, GoogleUpdate.exe) from user-writable
  directories such as %APPDATA%, %TEMP%, %PUBLIC% or Downloads. APT32 /
  OceanLotus drops these binaries together with a sibling malicious DLL
  (commonly rastls.dll, McUtil.dll, wsc.dll, goopdate.dll) to abuse the
  side-loading order and bypass signature controls.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/2018/03/13/oceanlotus-ships-new-backdoor/
  - https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2020/11/30/threat-actor-leverages-coin-miner-techniques-to-stay-under-the-radar/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1574.002
  - attack.t1036.005
  - attack.g0050
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\rastlsc.exe'
      - '\McOmonHost.exe'
      - '\wsc_proxy.exe'
      - '\SyLog.exe'
      - '\gup.exe'
      - '\GoogleUpdate.exe'
      - '\mcoemcpy.exe'
      - '\McTray.exe'
      - '\goopdate.exe'
  selection_path:
    Image|contains:
      - '\AppData\'
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\Users\Public\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
  filter_legit:
    Image|startswith:
      - 'C:\Program Files\'
      - 'C:\Program Files (x86)\'
      - 'C:\Windows\System32\'
      - 'C:\Windows\SysWOW64\'
  condition: selection_image and selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Software installers staging signed updaters in %TEMP%/%ProgramData% (verify the sibling DLL signature)
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\rastlsc.exe OR *\\RastlsC.exe OR *\\McOmonHost.exe OR *\\mcomonhost.exe OR *\\wsc_proxy.exe OR *\\WSC_Proxy.exe OR *\\SyLog.exe OR *\\sylog.exe OR *\\gup.exe OR *\\GUP.exe OR *\\GoogleUpdate.exe OR *\\googleupdate.exe OR *\\goopdate.exe OR *\\Goopdate.exe OR *\\mcoemcpy.exe OR *\\McTray.exe) AND @Image:(*\\AppData\\* OR *\\Downloads\\* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *\\Users\\Public\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\*) -@Image:(*\\Program Files\\* OR *\\Program Files (x86)\\* OR *\\Windows\\System32\\* OR *\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*) -@User:*$
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(rastlsc|mcomonhost|wsc_proxy|sylog|gup|googleupdate|goopdate|mcoemcpy|mctray)\.exe$/i
| regex("\\\\(AppData|Downloads|Temp|Public|ProgramData)\\\\", field=ImageFileName)
| NOT regex("\\\\Program Files( \\(x86\\))?\\\\", field=ImageFileName)
| NOT regex("\\\\Windows\\\\(System32|SysWOW64)\\\\", field=ImageFileName)
| join({#event_simpleName=ImageHash ImageFileName=/\.dll$/i | NOT regex("\\\\(Windows|Program Files)\\\\", field=ImageFileName)}, field=[aid, TargetProcessId], include=[ImageFileName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName, SHA256HashData], function=count(as=Hits))
| sort(Hits, order=desc)
ucs.rationale: DLL side-loading via signed third-party security vendor binaries is OceanLotus's most distinctive and persistently reused tradecraft — documented by ESET, FireEye/Mandiant, Cybereason (Operation Cobalt Kitty) and Microsoft (BISMUTH). The specific binary set (rastlsc.exe + rastls.dll, McOmonHost + McUtil, wsc_proxy + wsc.dll, SyLog/gup/GoogleUpdate variants) is consistently observed across Denis, K

ucs.title: [LLM] APT32 (OceanLotus) Outlook Home Page WebView persistence via HKCU Office registry hijack
ucs.description: Hunts OceanLotus's characteristic post-compromise persistence trick of writing an attacker-controlled HTTP(S) URL into the Outlook WebView / Today folder-home-page registry keys so that opening Outlook silently fetches and executes remote JScript/VBScript next-stage. This T1137-style abuse of the Office HKCU hive was documented by Volexity and ESET for APT32's Denis/KOMPROGO chains and is rarely seen outside Vietnam-aligned activity.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\Software\\Microsoft\\Office\\*" AND (Registry.registry_path IN ("*\\Outlook\\WebView\\*","*\\Outlook\\Today\\*","*\\Word\\Resiliency\\*","*\\Common\\Open Find\\*") OR Registry.registry_value_name IN ("URL","Page","Folder Home Page","WebView URL")) AND (Registry.registry_value_data="http://*" OR Registry.registry_value_data="https://*") by host Registry.user Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_name Registry.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
ucs.kql:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeySet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Microsoft\Office\"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Outlook\WebView", @"\Outlook\Today", @"\Word\Resiliency", @"\Common\Open Find")
      or RegistryValueName in~ ("URL","Page","Folder Home Page","WebView URL")
| where RegistryValueData startswith "http://" or RegistryValueData startswith "https://"
// OceanLotus typically writes the value from a non-Office process (PowerShell/script host)
// or from Office itself spawned by an exploited document
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","WINWORD.EXE","EXCEL.EXE","POWERPNT.EXE")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","cmd.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType =~ "RegistryValueSet"
| where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Microsoft\Office\"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Outlook\WebView", @"\Outlook\Today", @"\Word\Resiliency", @"\Common\Open Find")
      or RegistryValue in~ ("URL","Page","Folder Home Page","WebView URL")
| where RegistryValueData startswith "http://" or RegistryValueData startswith "https://"
| where ActingProcessName !has_any ("OUTLOOK.EXE","outlook.exe")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("powershell","wscript","cscript","mshta","rundll32","regsvr32")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: APT32 OceanLotus Outlook Home Page Persistence Via Office HKCU Registry
id: 6c8b7f02-eb5b-4d77-9d3e-2adf76e07c44
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects writes to Outlook WebView / Today / Word Resiliency / Office Common
  registry values under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Office that point at an http(s)
  URL. Used by APT32 (OceanLotus) to persist the Denis / KOMPROGO downloader
  family by abusing Outlook's folder-home-page feature so the next Outlook
  launch silently fetches remote JScript.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1137/
  - https://www.volexity.com/blog/2017/11/06/oceanlotus-blossoms-mass-digital-surveillance/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1137
  - attack.t1112
  - attack.g0050
logsource:
  category: registry_set
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_key:
    TargetObject|contains:
      - '\Software\Microsoft\Office\'
  selection_subkey:
    TargetObject|contains:
      - '\Outlook\WebView'
      - '\Outlook\Today'
      - '\Word\Resiliency'
      - '\Common\Open Find'
  selection_value:
    Details|startswith:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
  condition: selection_key and selection_subkey and selection_value
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate intranet Outlook folder home page pointing at an internal SharePoint URL (verify domain)
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\\Software\\Microsoft\\Office\\* AND (*\\Outlook\\WebView\\* OR *\\Outlook\\Today\\* OR *\\outlook\\webview\\* OR *\\outlook\\today\\* OR *\\Word\\Resiliency\\* OR *\\Common\\Open Find\\*)) @Details:(http://* OR https://*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate RegObjectName=/\\Software\\Microsoft\\Office\\.*\\(Outlook\\WebView|Outlook\\Today|Word\\Resiliency|Common\\Open Find)/i
| regex("^https?://", field=RegStringValue)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, RegObjectName, RegValueName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName], function=count(as=Hits))
| sort(Hits, order=desc)
ucs.rationale: Outlook WebView / folder-home-page persistence via HKCU registry is a niche T1137 sub-pattern that Volexity and ESET specifically attributed to APT32/OceanLotus during the Denis/KOMPROGO campaigns against ASEAN governments and Vietnamese dissidents. Most other crews favour Run-key or scheduled-task persistence; the Office registry path with an http(s) value is a high-purity OceanLotus tell. Generi
